tex_content.label: thm:local-section-theorem
tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Local Section Theorem] ↗ \cite{LeeSM} \dcref{chA:A.17} Suppose $M$ and $N$ are smooth manifolds and $\pi : M \to N$ is a smooth map. Then $\pi $ is a smooth submersion if and only if every point of $M$ is in the image of a smooth local section of $\pi $ (a map $\sigma : U \to M$ defined on some open subset $U \subseteq N$, with $\pi \circ \sigma = \text{Id}_U$).

The direction actually used below is that a submersion has local sections. It is formalized in the germ form that its consumers need: a map $\sigma $ defined and smooth near $\pi (p)$, with $\sigma (\pi (p)) = p$ and $\pi \circ \sigma = \mathrm{Id}$ on a neighbourhood of $\pi (p)$. The route below replaces Lee's appeal to the rank theorem (Theorem 5) by the inverse function theorem, which is cheaper and gives the same statement.
